subject: correlation between number of locations and occurrence areas

messages.author: b0eaaa355885abf4
messages.subject: correlation between number of locations and occurrence areas
parts:
Hi Christen

I calculated distribution occurrences for some birds using their location data, although the sample sizes are not very large (as few as 12 locations for some birds). After calculating the areas for these occurrence maps, I then calculated a correlation (spearman rank) between number of locations and areas from the occurrence maps. The correlation showed to be significant (0.6, p value 0.04). To me this makes sense because more number of locations could indeed mean that we have information to potentially calculate more areas. However I wonder if this also means my information is biased (?) Because then the area of occurrence could be biased by the number of locations the bird has.

Many thanks,

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: correlation between number of locations and occurrence areas
parts:
Hi Sandra,

Occurrence distributions are inherently sampling dependent. This is not bias unless they are being misused. The occurrence area is a measure of our uncertainty as to where the animal was during observation.

For a range-resident animal and fixed sampling frequency, you expect the occurrence area to increase to an asymptote with the number of locations.
For a dispersing animal and fixed sampling frequency, you expect the occurrence area to increase forever with the number of locations.

Best,
Chris
